summary: ELI LILLY AND COMPANY (LEI: FRDRIPF3EKNDJ2CQJL29; Indiana, US registration 183025-143) is identifier-confirmed across GLEIF, OpenCorporates, and Wikidata. GLEIF Level 2 data records no accounting-consolidation parent at either the direct or ultimate level, with permitted reporting exceptions filed on the basis that the entity is controlled by natural persons without an intermediate consolidating legal entity; this is a structural observation under LEI ROC policy and not an adverse finding. The company is recorded as the direct accounting-consolidation parent of at least six subsidiaries spanning the US, India, Ireland, the Netherlands, and the UK, and its key officers include David A. Ricks as CEO and board member (from 2017) and Jonathan Haug as senior managing official (from 2023), alongside a large board and officer cohort recorded in OpenCorporates and Wikidata. Two risk signals require further review: board member Katherine Baicker is a possible name match — unconfirmed by birth date or nationality — to a politically exposed person record on OpenSanctions and a political office-holder record on EveryPolitician (medium confidence each); and officer Christopher Anderson is matched at ICIJ score 100/100 to records in both the Panama Papers and the Paradise Papers (Appleby) (high confidence each), though these are name-based matches against related-party records and do not constitute findings of wrongdoing. A material gap exists: Wikirate could not be queried due to a source API schema error, so any data that source would have contributed is unavailable.

claims.text: ELI LILLY AND COMPANY is identifier-confirmed, registered in Indiana, United States, with LEI FRDRIPF3EKNDJ2CQJL29 and US-IN registration number 183025-143.

GLEIF Level 2 records accounting consolidation, not beneficial ownership; the natural-persons reporting exception means no named ultimate beneficial owner is disclosed in the LEI record.

PEP matches for Katherine Baicker and Patrik Jonsson are name-only matches with no corroborating identifiers (birth date, nationality); positive identification is not established.
The Panama Papers and Paradise Papers matches for Christopher Anderson are name-based and carry no corroborating identifiers confirming the related party is the same individual as the ICIJ record.
One board member is recorded in Wikidata only by a Wikidata QID (Q105798427) with no resolved name available in the packet.

risks.label: No parent in GLEIF (permitted reporting exception)
risks.rationale: No accounting-consolidation parent is reported to GLEIF: NATURAL_PERSONS for the direct and ultimate parent (the entity is controlled directly by natural person(s), with no intermediate legal entity that consolidates it — common for founder-, family-owned and widely held companies). Structural context, not a risk finding — these are permitted exceptions under the LEI ROC policy, and GLEIF Level 2 records accounting consolidation, not beneficial ownership.

risks.label: Outside EU/EEA
risks.rationale: Ownership chain reaches jurisdictions outside the EU/EEA: GB, IN, US-DE, US-IN. Structural context, not a risk finding — neither the AMLA CDD RTS nor AMLR Annex III treats non-EU status as a risk factor in itself. Contributes to AMLA Article 12(1) condition (b) only where it appears on the layered ownership path.
